::: {#sol-log-scale}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import numpy as np

even_rates = np.linspace(0.003, 3, 7)
print(even_rates.round(4))
```

Evenly spread rates go up by `r sprintf("%.4f", py$even_rates[2] - py$even_rates[1])` at each step,
so the second is already `r sprintf("%.4f", py$even_rates[2])`.
Nothing between 0.003 and that would be tried,
and that range holds [width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) 8's best [learning rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate), `r py$best_rate_8`,
and every rate at which width 512 was still improving in @fig-rate-sweep.
Good [learning rates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-learning-rate) can differ by factors of 10 or more,
so a sweep spaces them by a constant factor:
evenly on a log scale.
Random search draws a learning rate the same way,
uniform on its logarithm
([lds](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/ml-experimentation.html#tuning)).

:::
